cosine_findings.headline: Trust and Cooperation are roughly orthogonal at mean_trace (mean cos -0.13) but moderately aligned at last_trace (mean cos +0.51). They share output-space basis but diverge during reasoning.

steering_findings.headline: Applying the trust vector at PD-tuned layers (16, 25) on E4B yields WEAK steering: 12-26 pp dose-response range vs PD coop's 58 pp at the same cell. Direction is sometimes inverted (more alpha -> less trust at L16). Confirms the cosine result: PD-effective layers do not transfer to trust steering. A trust-tuned layer scan is needed.

calibration_curve_findings.headline: E4B is QUALITATIVELY CALIBRATED to payoff structure: trust rate rises from 0% at p*=0.10 (catastrophic downside) to 100% at p*=0.95 (freebie). Middle cells (p* 0.3-0.6) show noisy ~25-50% rates. Single outlier: high_upside (p*=0.75) gives 0% trust despite favorable EV.

trust_rate_vs_p_star.note: anomaly: zero trust despite favorable EV

calibration_curve_findings.note: Wide error bars due to small n=50 subset; with 30+ parsed stories per cell the curve would tighten. Catastrophic_betrayal cell (p*=0.02) absent from subset.

takeaways_for_paper: Trust is a mechanistically distinct direction from cooperation at mean_trace (cos ~0) — confirms procedural CAA methodology yields multiple axes.
Trust IS not effectively steered by PD-tuned layers — direct evidence that the steering vector's USEFUL layer is concept-specific, not model-specific. Layer choice matters per-concept.
E4B's trust calibration curve is qualitatively rational (rises monotonically with p* in 7/9 cells) but noisy at the middle, and has at least one cell where the model defies EV reasoning.

The trust direction at last_trace is partially aligned with cooperation (+0.51) — by the time the model emits the decision, prosocial intent collapses into a shared subspace. Reasoning-time representations diverge.
